messages.author: 4c1108aaddb5744d
messages.subject: multiple axes
parts:
Hi ggplot users,

I want to ask that how to make a multiple line-graph, and the scale of the multiple line can show in the left y-axis and right y-axis? For example, temperature and precipitation have different scales, so they can be drawn on the same graph but have different axes.
Or they can be on two graphs, while their x-axes can be lined up.

date             temperature  precipitation
2/1/2009             10                  0.6
2/2/2009             12                  0.8
2/3/2009             11                  0.9
2/4/2009             10                  1.0
2/5/2009             13                  1.2

Thanks very much.

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: multiple axes
parts:
Hi Lily, this has been addressed many times previously on the
listserv, but basically: ggplot2 doesn't support multiple axes like
this. For the "why" see Hadley's comments at e.g.
http://stackoverflow.com/a/3101876.

It is possible to fake this, but if you really need a dual-axis plot,
I'd recommend either thinking if you can use faceting instead, or
using another graphics package. Or fork ggplot and write the code
yourself... :)

HTH,

Ben

messages.author: 16584833d8a60e5e
messages.subject: Re: multiple axes
parts:
Bonjour,

Pour faire des diagramme ombrothermique j'utilise ce code :
Pluvio <- aggregate (formula = cbind(Precipitations) ~ Mois, data = db,
FUN= sum) # Données pluviométrie
TM <- aggregate (formula = cbind(TM) ~ Mois,data = db, FUN= mean) #
Données température


grid.newpage()
# Création de 2 graphiques
p1 <- ggplot(TM, aes(x=Mois,y=TM)) +
geom_line(colour = "red", size = 1.2, linetype = 1) +
scale_x_continuous (limits = c(1,12), breaks = c(1:12),
label=c("Janvier",
"Février","Mars","Avril","Mai","Juin","Juillet","Aout","Septembre","Octobre","Novembre","Décembre"
)) +
scale_y_continuous (name = "Température en C°",limits = c(0,60),
breaks = c(0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60)) +
theme_gray()+
theme(panel.grid.minor.x=element_blank(),
panel.grid.major.x=element_blank())
p1 <- p1 + labs(title = "Diagramme Ombrothermique 2013")
#p1

p2 <- ggplot(Pluvio, aes(x=Mois,y=Precipitations)) +
geom_bar (aes(fill=Precipitations),stat = "identity", alpha = 0.6) +
#geom_text(aes(label = Pluvio), colour="Blue") +
scale_x_continuous ( breaks = c(1:12),
label= c("Janvier",
"Février","Mars","Avril","Mai","Juin","Juillet","Aout","Septembre","Octobre","Novembre","Décembre"
)) +
scale_y_continuous ( limits = c(0,120), breaks = c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80,
100, 120)) +
theme_gray () %+replace%
theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, size = 0.1, linetype
= 0.5)) +
theme(panel.grid.minor.x=element_blank(),
panel.grid.major.x=element_blank())
#p2

# Création d'objet à partir des graphiques
g1 <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(p1))
g2 <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(p2))

# Fusion des 2 graphiques selon conditions
pp <- c(subset(g1$layout, name == "panel", se = t:r))
g <- gtable_add_grob(g1, g2$grobs[[which(g2$layout$name == "panel")]],
pp$t, pp$l, pp$b, pp$r)

# Réglage des axes
ia <- which(g2$layout$name == "axis-l")
ga <- g2$grobs[[ia]]
ax <- ga$children[[2]]
ax$widths <- rev(ax$widths)
ax$grobs <- rev(ax$grobs)
ax$grobs[[1]]$x <- ax$grobs[[1]]$x - unit(1, "npc") + unit(0.1, "cm")

# Positionnement des graphiques sur les axes
g <- gtable_add_cols(g, g2$widths[g2$layout[ia, ]$l], length(g$widths) - 1)
g <- gtable_add_grob(g, ax, pp$t, length(g$widths) - 1, pp$b)


# Affichage des graphiques
grid.draw(g)


Bonne continuation
Lionel

Lionel JULIEN
UMR SELMET
Système d'Elevage Méditerranéen et Tropicaux
campus international de Baillarguet
